lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Claudette, it's Daniela from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the vegetables went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your energy been this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So-so. Up and down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 5 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Honestly, not much. I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you buy frozen vegetables?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, finding the time makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Just cut out the rice. That's the easiest thing.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You feel like you have to do something.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Frozen vegetables count just as much as fresh, and they're cheaper.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I bought spinach and actually used it. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Beans count too, and they keep you full.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Half your plate has to be vegetables. That's the rule.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everything at the store costs so much.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the cost gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I'll do it right when I wake up, before anything else.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: finding the time made this week harder, you still got 0 days in, and your plan is to add a vegetable to lunch and dinner on 3 days. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Reflects feeling of needing to act
Beans count and fill you up
Asks for backup plan for cost
Plans to eat vegetables on waking

flags.reason: Unsolicited directive 'Just cut out the rice' right after the participant voiced resistance.
'You have to make this a priority' pushes advice; participant replied 'Maybe'.
Health-threat warning; repeated persuading with persuading pattern across lines 18, 26, 28, 40.
Rule-based directive ('That's the rule') without asking permission; participant was raising cost barrier.
Participant's plan to eat vegetables on waking was not reinforced or explored.
Participant said they used spinach and liked it; coach did not affirm or explore this success.

score.summary: The coach reviewed the last goal and set a new one, but repeatedly used directives (lines 18, 26, 28, 40) that met resistance with 'Maybe' and 'Sometimes'. Change talk at lines 25, 29, 33 and 43 was not consistently reinforced, and no next contact was set.
strengths: Reviewed last goal and summarized the plan (lines 8, 44).
Affirmed the fridge reminder effort: 'That's real progress.' (line 14).
Asked permission before sharing ideas (lines 30, 34) and offered frozen and bean options as information (lines 32, 36).
Used a complex reflection to name ambivalence (line 16).
coaching_tips: Replace 'Just cut out the rice' (line 18) and 'You have to make this a priority' (line 26) with an open question about what the participant thinks might help.
Reinforce the spinach success at line 33 with an affirmation and ask what made it work.
Respond to the change talk at line 43 with a reflection and affirmation rather than moving straight to a summary.
Avoid warnings like 'your health is going to suffer' (line 28); reflect the participant's own reason for change, such as not wanting cancer back (line 19).
Set a specific next contact date and time before closing; none was set.
